name: RPF Constable
conductingBody: Railway Recruitment Boards on behalf of the Railway Protection Force (Ministry of Railways)
approxCandidates: ≈45 lakh+ applicants in the CEN RPF 02/2024 cycle (approx.)
eligibility: 10th (Matriculation) pass; 18–28 yrs (relaxation as per rules); physical standards apply

notification.summary: No new RPF Constable notification had been released as of 10 Oct 2026. The last cycle, CEN RPF 02/2024 (≈4,208 Constable posts), held its CBT in March 2025; its CBT result was declared and the PET/PMT, DV and medical stages ran in 2026 as reported. Reports in 2026 expect the next Constable/SI notification, but no official date or vacancy count has been announced.

pattern.notes: No sectional timing; 1/3 negative marking; marks normalised across shifts. Qualifying: UR/OBC/EWS 35%, SC/ST 30%. CBT shortlists candidates for PET (1600 m run for men / 800 m for women, long jump, high jump) and PMT, followed by DV and medical. Questions are of Class 10 standard.

trendAnalysis.summary: Only two recent Constable CBTs exist (CEN 01/2018, held Dec 2018–Feb 2019, and CEN RPF 02/2024, held Mar 2025), so the analysis is based on both. The paper is easy-to-moderate. General Awareness (50 Q) is the largest section: around a fifth is current affairs (sports, awards, schemes), with the rest static GK – history, polity, geography, general science and culture. Arithmetic is direct (number system, percentage, average, profit-loss, SI/CI, time-speed-distance, mensuration). Reasoning is scoring with analogies, series, coding, blood relations, ranking and simple puzzles; non-verbal items (mirror image, embedded figures) appear in small numbers. Good attempts are around 95–105 of 120.

pyqBlueprint.method: Only two Constable CBTs exist in the window: CEN 01/2018 (CBT Dec 2018–Feb 2019) and CEN RPF 02/2024 (CBT 2–18 Mar 2025); no Constable CBT was held in 2026, so the blueprint covers 2019 and 2025 (matching trendAnalysis.yearsAnalyzed). RRB barred sharing of live questions; web searches (Oct 2026) returned only shift-wise difficulty/good-attempt analyses (Adda247, PracticeMock, Careerpower, Prepp) without question-level detail, and WebFetch of papers was not possible. Question TYPES were described from the writer's own knowledge of the 2018–19 papers and the 2025 memory-based topic lists. All patterns are paraphrased.

archetypes.pattern: Sports results of the last year – tournament winners, medal tallies, players' home states
National events – new laws, state firsts, mega events and their venues
Appointments, summits and awards in the news
Freedom struggle – INC sessions, leaders' titles and newspapers, commissions and incidents
Ancient and medieval rulers, dynasty founders and monuments
Articles for rights/remedies/impeachment and constitutional heads – oath, appointment, powers
Parliament – composition, nominated members, age qualifications
Indian lakes, rivers, dams and national parks – state or river they belong to
World geography – oceans, continents, superlatives
Banks and financial institutions – headquarters and functions (RBI, NABARD)
Biology – photosynthesis, vitamins, blood and human body
Physics/chemistry in daily life – metals, instruments, units
Dances, festivals and sports terms/team sizes
Important days, books and authors, founding years of organisations
Computer basics – devices, abbreviations, memory
Railways and RPF basics – controlling ministry, RPF Act, railway facts
Divisibility tests and least number to subtract/add for divisibility
Primes in a range, sum of primes/consecutive numbers
BODMAS with decimals and fractions
HCF × LCM product rule, lights/bells changing together
x% of a number, finding the number, "A more than B → B less than A"
Expenditure out of income in stages – find salary/savings
Ratio with a difference/addition condition – find the numbers or total
Consecutive numbers, adding/removing a member and its effect on average
Profit % from CP/SP, buy-n-sell-at-price, successive discounts
SI for years and months, doubling time; CI half-yearly
Two or three persons working together
Speed conversion, train crossing a pole, late/early arrival with changed speed
Rectangle/circle perimeter and area (fencing cost), cuboid volume in litres
Right triangles (Pythagoras, perpendicular), triangle angle sums with algebraic angles
Small table of monthly/yearly figures – percentage change or average
Word analogy – animal/young one, creature/dwelling, worker/tool
Number analogy – n(n+1), n³ ± 1, n² relations
Odd word out from a category (units, crops, instruments)
Odd number pair out (n : n³, n : n/2, etc.)
Number series with ×2, ×2 + 1 or doubling differences
Letter-cluster series with fixed forward/backward steps
Uniform letter shift (+k) coding of a word
Opposite-letter (A↔Z, B↔Y) or reverse-order coding
Symbol/letter substitution and BODMAS evaluation
Short relation chains – how is A related to B
Two- or three-leg walks – shortest distance and direction
Two statements with two conclusions (All/Some/No)
Linear row of 5–6 people facing one direction
Two-set counting (both/only/neither) and class-relationship diagrams
Statement with two conclusions about a person/policy
Ranks from top/bottom or left/right – total count or position
Missing number in bracketed groups/rows with a² + b², a × b type rules
Mirror image of a clock/word and paper folding–punching (count holes); embedded figures in the figure-based shifts

resources.notes: For CEN RPF 02/2024 the question papers, provisional answer keys and response sheets were made available by the RRBs only during the objection window via regional RRB websites (linked from https://www.rrbapply.gov.in). RPF notices are also posted at https://rpf.indianrailways.gov.in. No permanent official PYQ archive; memory-based papers from coaching publishers are unofficial.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹7,500 at 6% per annum for 2 years 6 months?

relevance.note: SI for years and months - RPF exact

questions.question: A, B and C can complete a work in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. In how many days can they complete it working together?
questions.explanation: One day's work = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15 = (6 + 5 + 4)/60 = 15/60 = 1/4. So they finish in 4 days.

relevance.note: Three workers together - RPF

questions.question: A train running at 90 km/h crosses a pole in 12 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: 90 km/h = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s. Length = 25 × 12 = 300 m. (Not converting units gives 1080.)

relevance.note: Train length crossing pole - RPF

questions.question: Walking at 4/5 of his usual speed, a man reaches his office 15 minutes late. What is his usual time to reach the office?
questions.explanation: At 4/5 of the speed he takes 5/4 of the usual time. Extra time = 1/4 of usual time = 15 min, so usual time = 60 minutes.

relevance.note: Late arrival with reduced speed fraction - RPF exact

questions.question: A rectangular water tank is 6 m long, 4 m wide and 2.5 m deep. How many litres of water can it hold when full?
questions.explanation: Volume = 6 × 4 × 2.5 = 60 m³. Since 1 m³ = 1000 litres, capacity = 60,000 litres.

relevance.note: Cuboid tank in litres with ×1000 traps - RPF exact archetype

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are (2x)°, (3x + 10)° and (4x − 10)°. What is the measure of its largest angle?
questions.explanation: 2x + 3x + 10 + 4x − 10 = 180 → 9x = 180 → x = 20. The angles are 40°, 70° and 70°, so the largest angle is 70°.

relevance.note: Algebraic triangle angles - RPF

questions.question: The number of passengers (in thousands) using a train service in four months was: January 24, February 30, March 36, April 30. By what percentage did the number in March exceed that in January?
questions.explanation: Increase = 36 − 24 = 12 thousand on a base of 24 thousand: 12/24 × 100 = 50%. (Dividing by 36 gives 33.33%.)

relevance.note: Small passenger table % change - RPF DI-lite

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.
Cow : Calf :: Horse : ?
questions.explanation: The young one of a cow is a calf; the young one of a horse is a foal. (Kid – goat, cub – lion, puppy – dog.)

relevance.note: Animal:young one Horse:Foal - RPF exact

questions.question:
Select the number that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.
3 : 28 :: 4 : ?
questions.explanation: 3³ + 1 = 28. Similarly 4³ + 1 = 65.

relevance.note: n³+1 analogy - RPF

questions.question: Select the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Kilogram, quintal and tonne are units of mass; litre is a unit of volume.

relevance.note: Litre volume among mass units - RPF units odd-one

questions.question: Select the odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: In the other pairs the second number is half of the first. Half of 30 is 15, not 16.

relevance.note: n:n/2 odd pair is very easy; RPF pairs typically need some computation

questions.question:
Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series?
6, 9, 15, 27, 51, ?
questions.explanation: Differences double: +3, +6, +12, +24, +48. So 51 + 48 = 99.

relevance.note: Doubling differences series - RPF

questions.question:
Select the letter-cluster that will come next in the following series.
AYB, CWD, EUF, ?
questions.explanation: First letters: A, C, E, G (+2); middle letters: Y, W, U, S (−2); last letters: B, D, F, H (+2). Next = GSH.

relevance.note: Three-letter cluster forward/backward steps - RPF

questions.question: In a certain code language, PLANT is written as RNCPV. How will GREEN be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is moved 2 places forward: P→R, L→N, A→C, N→P, T→V. So G→I, R→T, E→G, E→G, N→P = ITGGP.

relevance.note: Uniform +2 coding - RPF

questions.question: In a certain code language, GOLD is written as TLOW. How will SILVER be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter (A↔Z, B↔Y …; position p → 27 − p): G→T, O→L, L→O, D→W. So S→H, I→R, L→O, V→E, E→V, R→I = HROEVI.

relevance.note: Opposite-letter coding - RPF exact

questions.question:
If '×' means '÷', '÷' means '+', '+' means '−' and '−' means '×', what is the value of the following expression?
36 × 4 ÷ 5 − 3 + 10

relevance.note: Symbol substitution BODMAS - RPF

questions.question: A's mother is the sister of B's father. How is A related to B?
questions.explanation: A's mother is B's paternal aunt, so A is the child of B's aunt – B's cousin. (A's gender is not known, so 'nephew' or 'brother' cannot be right.)

relevance.note: Father's sister's child cousin - RPF short chain

questions.question: Raman walks 20 m towards the north, then turns left and walks 15 m. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Turning left from north means walking west. He is 20 m north and 15 m west of the start: distance = √(20² + 15²) = 25 m, towards the North-West.

relevance.note: Two-leg walk 15-20-25 NW - RPF

questions.question:
Statements:
All doctors are graduates.
No graduate is illiterate.
Conclusions:
I. No doctor is illiterate.
II. Some graduates are doctors.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Doctors lie inside graduates and no graduate is illiterate, so no doctor is illiterate (I). "All doctors are graduates" implies "Some graduates are doctors" (II). Both follow.

relevance.note: All-No syllogism both follow - RPF

questions.question: Five persons A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. C sits exactly in the middle. A sits to the immediate right of C. E sits at the extreme right end. B does not sit at the extreme left end. Who sits at the extreme left end?
questions.explanation: Positions from the left: C = 3, A = 4, E = 5. B and D take positions 1 and 2; B is not at the left end, so D = 1.

relevance.note: 5-person row - RPF

questions.question: In a village of 500 people, 300 speak Hindi and 250 speak Marathi. Every person speaks at least one of the two languages. How many people speak only Hindi?

relevance.note: Only Hindi from at-least-one data - RPF counting

questions.question: In a class, Rita ranks 7th from the top. Gita is 5 ranks below Rita and is 21st from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
questions.explanation: Gita's rank from the top = 7 + 5 = 12. Total = 12 + 21 − 1 = 32.

relevance.note: Rank chain to total - RPF

questions.question:
Find the missing number.
8 (40) 5
9 (54) 6
7 (?) 8
questions.explanation: The middle number is the product of the outer numbers: 8 × 5 = 40, 9 × 6 = 54, so 7 × 8 = 56.

relevance.note: Bracket product rule - RPF missing number

questions.question: A wall clock shows the time 8:25. What time will its image in a plane mirror (placed vertically) show?
questions.explanation: Mirror time = 11:60 − actual time = 11:60 − 8:25 = 3:35.

relevance.note: Mirror clock 8:25 → 3:35 - RPF

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded in half from top to bottom and then folded in half again from left to right. A single hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when the sheet is completely unfolded?
questions.explanation: Two folds make 4 layers. A punch through all layers makes one hole in each layer, i.e. 4 holes after unfolding.

relevance.note: Paper folded twice punched once → 4 holes - RPF folding-punching (text version of figure item)
